components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one primary action on a screen: sign in/up, continue lesson, continue onboarding.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #10B981; color: #FFFFFF; height: 52px; padding: 0 24px; border-radius: 16px; border: none; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700; transition: opacity 0.15s ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: 0.9; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #047857; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { background: #E5E7EB; color: #9CA3AF; }

components.name: Card Surface
components.description: Base card used for the dashboard progress card, auth form, and profile card.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #FFFFFF; border: 1px solid #E5E7EB; border-radius: 24px; padding: 24px; } .ds-card-title { font-size: 18px; font-weight: 800; color: #111827; margin-bottom: 8px; } .ds-card-body { font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; color: #6B7280; }

components.name: XP Badge Pill
components.description: Rounded stat pill used for XP and streak counts in the dashboard header.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; background: #ECFDF5; border: 1px solid #A7F3D0; color: #047857; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; padding: 8px 12px; border-radius: 999px; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Auth-screen field with an uppercase tracked label above it rather than an inline placeholder-only pattern.
components.css: .ds-field-label { display: block; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.5px; color: #6B7280; margin-bottom: 8px; } .ds-input { width: 100%; height: 52px; background: #F9FAFB; border: 1.5px solid #E5E7EB; border-radius: 14px; padding: 0 16px; font-size: 15px; color: #111827; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #9CA3AF; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #10B981; outline-offset: 1px; border-color: #10B981; }

components.name: Quiz Option
components.description: Selectable quiz answer row with three feedback states (selected/blue, correct/emerald, wrong/red) layered on the same flat-bordered base shape.
components.html: <button class="ds-quiz-option ds-quiz-option--selected">To map out and control your cash flow</button>
components.css: .ds-quiz-option { display: block; width: 100%; text-align: left; background: #FFFFFF; border: 2px solid #E5E7EB; border-radius: 16px; padding: 18px 20px; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700; color: #4B5563; transition: border-color 0.15s ease-out, background 0.15s ease-out; } .ds-quiz-option--selected { border-color: #3B82F6; background: #EFF6FF; color: #1D4ED8; } .ds-quiz-option--correct { border-color: #10B981; background: #ECFDF5; color: #1F2937; } .ds-quiz-option--wrong { border-color: #EF4444; background: #FEF2F2; color: #1F2937; }

components.name: Progress Bar
components.description: The single most-repeated component: level progress, module progress, and lesson-slide progress all use this same track+fill shape.
components.css: .ds-progress-track { height: 12px; background: #E5E7EB; border-radius: 6px; overflow: hidden; } .ds-progress-fill { height: 100%; background: #10B981; border-radius: 6px; transition: width 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); }

components.name: Bottom Tab Bar
components.description: Flat bottom navigation with emoji icons, zero shadow, and a single top hairline border.
components.css: .ds-tabbar { display: flex; justify-content: space-around; align-items: center; height: 56px; padding-top: 6px; padding-bottom: 8px; background: #FFFFFF; border-top: 1px solid #E5E7EB; box-shadow: none; } .ds-tab { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; text-align: center; color: #9CA3AF; } .ds-tab--active { color: #10B981; }

narrative.overview: finlit's whole visual system sits on a deliberate tension: the mechanics are pure playground — streaks, XP, levels, a lesson that ends in a trophy emoji and a spring-animated badge — but the shell around them is calm, bordered, and quiet. Nothing about the surface shouts. Cards are flat with a hairline border rather than a shadow; type leans heavy (700-800 weight) for confidence rather than loud for attention; the one saturated color in the whole system is a single emerald green that means "growth" everywhere it appears. That restraint is what lets the game-like parts read as credible instead of gimmicky — this is still an app about someone's money. This system explicitly rejects the stuffy-bank-app look (no navy-and-gold, no dense tables, no cold institutional distance) and the generic-AI-dashboard look (no cream/gray card grids, no decorative gradients). Warmth comes from color use, rounded shapes, and copy tone — not from a tinted neutral background pretending to be "friendly."
keyCharacteristics: Flat surfaces, hairline borders — depth is a border and a background shift, not a shadow.
One accent, many jobs: Growth Emerald marks progress, success, active state, and the one primary action per screen.
Heavy type weight (700-800) does the hierarchy work; size varies less than weight does.
Generous, consistent roundness (14-24px on containers, full-round on pills/avatars) — nothing sharp-cornered.
Emoji as illustration. There is no icon library in use; emoji carry all iconography and decorative imagery.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Growth Emerald is the only saturated color allowed to represent a positive/active state. Don't introduce a second "brand" color; every other hue in the system exists to mark one specific, narrow state (streak = amber, danger = red, quiz-selected = blue) and appears nowhere else.

rules.name: The Weight-Over-Size Rule
rules.body: When something needs to feel more important, make it heavier (600 → 700 → 800), not bigger. The type scale only spans 12-32px across the entire app; 800-weight at 15px (a button) reads as confident, not small.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: If you're reaching for a shadow anywhere other than the ambient brand glow or the toggle thumb, use a border and a surface-color shift instead. Shadow in this system means "this is a physical toggle" or "this is the brand mark," not "this is elevated content."

dos: Do use Growth Emerald (#10B981) as the only accent carrying meaning — progress, success, active state, primary action.
Do build hierarchy with font-weight (500→800) before reaching for a bigger size.
Do keep cards and rows flat with a 1-1.5px Hairline Border; reserve shadow for the two named exceptions (splash glow, toggle thumb).
Do pair every state color with both a background tint and a matching border — never a bare-border accent.
Do keep every screen consuming useTheme() tokens so light/dark mode stays correct app-wide.
donts: Don't design anything that reads as "a stuffy corporate bank app" — no navy-and-gold, no dense data tables, no cold institutional distance.
Don't add a second saturated "brand" accent alongside Growth Emerald — every other hue in this system is scoped to one narrow state and nothing else.
Don't use border-left/border-right as a colored accent stripe anywhere.
Don't hardcode hex colors in a screen file — every screen (including LessonScreen, migrated to theme tokens) pulls color from useTheme().colors so dark mode stays correct everywhere.
Don't add drop shadows to cards or buttons "for depth" — flat + border is the system's answer to depth, not shadow.
